target: Six unchanged native quadratic source reads from MLP16 feeding three later components. Native z and later h remain supplied.
question: Can an invertible linear input change expose disjoint source-coordinate blocks shared by all six forms?
method: Simple regular pencil A=sum a_o T_o, B=sum b_o T_o; diagonalize A^-1 B, transform every A^-1 T_o, and find connected components of their off-diagonal coupling graph. A connected graph forces scalar center under the checked simple-spectrum assumption.
prior_art: Earlier pair pencil test only obstructed real simultaneous squares for two low-dimensional cores. This tests multi-form block congruence on all six full1152 forms.
pred_a: All four pencils simple and adequately conditioned; residuals <1e-10, normalized minimum eigengap>1e-10, anchor/eigenbasis conditions<1e8. Otherwise INCONCLUSIVE, not negative structure result.
pred_b: Nontrivial source split: >1 graph component in all four screens at threshold1e-8. Opposing null: connected graph/scalar center, so no exact congruence direct sum in this numerical screen.
pred_c: Same component sizes under invertible covariance coordinate change for each fixed pencil seed. Mismatch invalidates structural interpretation until diagnosed.
controls: Five planted nonorthogonal congruences recover known block sizes and independent dense-center nullities. Degenerate pencil explicitly rejected. Already passed before native execution.
cost: O(o*d^3) dense solves/eigen/transforms, O(o*d^2) memory, CPU2threads. No new calibration or behavioral selection. A successful exact split proposes smaller independent source programs; full products/storage and native intervention still required.
limits: Numerical, not interval-certified. Disconnected complex blocks require real conjugate assembly; no real compiler claimed. A negative result does not rule out overlapping features, approximate circuits, or general DAG reuse.
